LANDFIRE Program · USDA Forest Service & DOI Wildland Fire Service

Acronym Reference

Companion to The LANDFIRE Dependency Web. Every acronym appearing in that diagram is defined here, grouped by where it sits in the flow — the agencies behind the data, the inputs LANDFIRE ingests, the layers LANDFIRE produces, and the tools and programs that depend on them.

Dependent Tools, Models & Programs

BlueSky
Smoke modeling framework linking fuels, consumption and dispersion
Consume
Fuel consumption and emissions model
CWDG
Community Wildfire Defense Grant
CWPP
Community Wildfire Protection Plan
FARSITE
Fire Area Simulator
FastFuels
3D fuels dataset and generator for fire behavior modeling
FlamMap
Fire behavior mapping and analysis system
FSim
Large Fire Simulator
FSPro
Fire Spread Probability model
IFMAT
Assessment of Indian Forests and Forest Management
IFTDSS
Interagency Fuel Treatment Decision Support System
NEPA
National Environmental Policy Act
POD
Potential Operational Delineation
RPA
Resources Planning Act — periodic national assessment of renewable resources
SDI
Suppression Difficulty Index
TCA
Terrestrial Condition Assessment
TreeMap
Modeled tree-level forest inventory mapped nationally from FIA plots
VSmoke
Screening model for smoke dispersion from prescribed burns
WFDSS
Wildland Fire Decision Support System
WindNinja
Wind field model for complex terrain
WUI
Wildland-Urban Interface
Note: Agency attributions in the dependency web appear in braces, e.g. {USGS}, and indicate the organization that produces or stewards the dataset — not necessarily its sole contributor. Where a dataset is jointly produced, contributing agencies are separated by an ampersand.
